doc.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: Father's guitar and mandolin and music at home
summary: His father played guitar and mandolin in Sicilian serenading groups; the only musician in the family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Was there a lot of music around the house in your family?

My father, but he was the only one really, guitar and mandolin. He was the only one. And he played, he wasn’t studied. He came over from Italy, they used to have a group called The Troubadors. They used to go around and play under ladies’ windows you know, and traveled through Sicily. But then there was other people that they followed up with a group in Tarrytown, and they used to break into houses at four o’clock in the morning and the women had to cook them coffee while they played. So there was a lot of music around, but in my family it was just my father.
Did he encourage you to go into music, or why did you choose music as a career?
